text: Solar Benchmarks 是一款面向 DSH Web 客户端的基准测试插件，在会话界面提供基准目录、实验配置、运行记录与对照分析。它注册公开数据集和内置任务、评分器及运行管理器，可选择模型、抽样任务和待比较插件，执行基线对比并记录成功率、耗时与成本。用户还能查看实验账本、跨版本趋势和插件运行痕迹。适合希望系统评估 DSH 插件效果的开发者。使用 DeepSeek 驱动、裁判评分或网页工具时需要配置 DEEPSEEK_API_KEY；公开基准数据会按需从 Hugging Face 等来源获取。

Solar Benchmarks adds benchmark setup, run records, and comparison views to DSH. Users select tasks, a model, and plugins, then compare results with a baseline. DeepSeek drivers or judge scoring require DEEPSEEK_API_KEY; public data is fetched on demand.

Solar Benchmarks 的功能「配置并运行实验」：在基准目录选择可运行的任务、抽样数量、模型和要比较的插件，提交后在界面查看进度并可停止运行。
Solar Benchmarks 的功能「对照分析」：把插件组与无插件基线的配对结果展示为成功率、统计结论、成本和速度，并按基准任务查看表现。
Solar Benchmarks 的功能「查询实验记录」：界面保存并展示各次实验的运行账本；注册的 bench_results、bench_compare 和 bench_trace 工具可供 DSH agent 查询结果、比较与运行详情。
Solar Benchmarks 使用裁判评分时会把评分提示和模型回答发送到配置的 DeepSeek 聊天补全接口；该接口请求使用 DEEPSEEK_API_KEY。见 src/judge.ts:29-38。
Solar Benchmarks 会按实验需要从 Hugging Face 或固定版本文件来源获取公开基准数据。见 src/datasets.ts:91-110。

@lisihao/dsh-solar-bench README · Solar Benchmarks：Unreleased source candidate: `@lisihao/dsh-solar-bench`. It runs recognized public benchmarks, grouped by category, against DSH with a fixed model, compares a baseline without third-party plugins against runs with each chosen plugin, stops at a spending limit, keeps every run in a versioned ledger, and analyzes across experiments whether plugins load, help, and change cost or time. Every run is an isolated `dsh` one-shot child process. The design and the source of every catalog entry are in [docs/benchmarks-design.md](docs/benchmarks-design.md).

@lisihao/dsh-solar-bench README · Install：Quit the app, then install with the app's bundled CLI into the Desktop profile (the app may live in `/Applications` or `~/Applications`):

```bash
"/Applications/DeepSeek Harness.app/Contents/Resources/runtime/cli/bin/dsh" plugin --profile desktop add github:lisihao/dsh-solar-bench
```

Relaunch the app. Running an experiment calls the chosen model provider and can cost money; the form shows the spending limit before it starts.

@lisihao/dsh-solar-bench README · Using it in the app：Open any started conversation. Its View tab bar (next to Chat and Trajectory) has a **基准测试 / Benchmarks** tab. rc.2 draws that bar only for a started Session with at least two Views, and remembers the chosen View per Session.

The page has four tabs, each a keyboard-reachable tab row that wraps inside its own box at narrow widths:

@lisihao/dsh-solar-bench README · Using it in the app：**Evidence of use** (roadmap 2.3). A compared plugin that loaded but left no trace in its runs reads **未测到 / Not tested** instead of a verdict, so a loaded-but-idle plugin is never reported as "no difference". Each run records its `surface` from the session log: every tool offered to the model in the root session's `request/header` events with a short SHA-256 of its schema, a SHA-256 of the root session's system prompts, a SHA-256 of the opening context (the user and developer messages before the first assistant message, with the run's own directory replaced by a placeholder), and counts of `hook/invoked`, `model/selection`, `compaction/start` and `developer/message` events across all sessions. The analysis counts a plugin run as exercised when a tool the baseline was never offered was called, a tool the baseline was offered too carried a different schema (a plugin that rewrites tool descriptions), its system prompt matches no baseline run, its opening context differs from the baseline run of the same item (a plugin that replaces the skill catalog or adds recalled memory), or it logged more of one of those events than that run.

@lisihao/dsh-solar-bench README · Using it in the app：With no runs yet, the run records, comparisons and diagnosis tabs offer a start with GSM8K in the library. A warning on every tab counts ledgers that could not be read.

@lisihao/dsh-solar-bench README · Using it in the app：- **Configure and run** on a runnable card: items to sample and a seed, repetitions, a **required budget in US dollars**, the driver, the plugins to compare (none runs the baseline alone), whether web tools are allowed, and whether runs include the user's global skills (unchecked by default; check it to mirror daily use). The plan line shows the number of runs; the estimate uses only the recorded mean cost of that benchmark, driver and global-skills setting, and says so when there is no history. **开始运行（会调用模型并产生费用）** starts it. It needs the DeepSeek API key saved on the Models settings page.
- **The run panel** appears as soon as a run is accepted and stays pinned at the top of the page while it scrolls. It shows the state (sampling, running, finished, stopped, failed), progress, spend against the budget, the run in progress, one square per finished run, the log and **停止**. Sampling and setup happen after the start is accepted, so a slow or failed fetch shows in the panel. While a run is going, the form says so instead of offering to start. The panel shows on every tab. @lisihao/dsh-solar-bench README · Benchmarks that run here：| Category | Benchmark | Graded by |
|---|---|---|
| Agents & tool calling | BFCL v3 `simple` | BFCL's AST rule on a JSON call written in the final message |
| Programming | HumanEval, HumanEval+, MBPP (sanitized) | the dataset's tests against `solution.py`, under the app's bundled Python 3.12 |
| General | MMLU-Pro, ARC-Challenge, BIG-Bench Hard | final `ANSWER:` line (letter, or normalized exact match) |
| General | SimpleQA | judge model with the simple-evals grader template |
| Mathematics | GSM8K, AIME 2024, AIME 2025 | numeric equality |
| Mathematics | MATH-500 | normalized string or numeric equality (stricter than symbolic equivalence) |
| Long context | LongBench v2 | letter; the document is written to `context.txt` in the workspace |
| Preference | MT-Bench, first turn | judge model, MT-Bench `single-v1` / `single-math-v1`, 1–10 |
| AI for Science | LAB-Bench (LitQA2, SeqQA, ProtocolQA), ChemBench (multiple choice), ScienceQA (text-only) | letter |
| Harness comparison | DSH native repository tasks (bundled, not a public benchmark) | command exit, file contents, tool use |

@lisihao/dsh-solar-bench README · Benchmarks that run here：Rows are fetched when an experiment starts — Hugging Face datasets-server for parquet datasets (only the sampled rows), or whole files at a pinned commit — and never shipped with the plugin. A rate-limited or failed request (429, 5xx) is retried up to five times, honoring `Retry-After`.

@lisihao/dsh-solar-bench README · Floor and ceiling：Every catalog row carries an editorial tier, shown as a pill on its card and in the scoreboard: **保底 / Floor** benchmarks are expected to sit near full marks with the default driver, so a run checks that nothing got worse; **摸高 / Ceiling** benchmarks leave room for a plugin to show a gain. The tiers are a classification as of 2026-10-30, not a measurement; one benchmark listed in two categories (SWE-bench Verified) has one tier.

@lisihao/dsh-solar-bench README · Floor and ceiling：**已饱和 / Saturated** is the measured part: a pass-rate benchmark is marked saturated when, in a baseline cell from its row's latest experiment, the items that passed on every valid run give a one-sided 95% Clopper–Pearson lower bound of at least 90% (all 29 of 29 items is the smallest sample that clears it; 10 of 10 gives about 74%). It counts items, not runs, since repetitions of one item are not independent. Cells from earlier experiments (the † cells) and judged mean scores never count. The badge never changes the declared tier.

@lisihao/dsh-solar-bench README · Floor and ceiling：The **递归自我改进（RSI）** tab lists RSI-Exam (`RSI-Exam/RSI-Exam`, MIT, revision `66f5493`): of its 35 public tasks, 25 declare `gpus = 0` (the other 10 omit the field, which RSI-Exam's GPU guide prescribes for GPU tasks), and 4 of those call a model from inside the task; the remaining 21 are in scope, up to 12 hours each. Its tasks run in Docker containers through Harbor (see Container benchmarks below); the card says what this computer still lacks. Its best published mean, 0.464, is over all 88 tasks and is not comparable to a CPU-only subset.

@lisihao/dsh-solar-bench README · Container benchmarks (Harbor)：RSI-Exam runs through [Harbor](https://github.com/laude-institute/harbor) 0.25.0 with DSH as the agent. The design is `docs/integrations/harbor.md` in the V4 repository; pins and the APIs relied on are in `UPGRADING.md`.

@lisihao/dsh-solar-bench README · Drivers：The judge of a judged benchmark is chosen separately (DeepSeek models, through the DeepSeek API), so a local or subscription driver can still run SimpleQA and MT-Bench. Only the keys an experiment uses are resolved; the DeepSeek key is needed for a DeepSeek driver, a judge, or web tools (the run profile's search and fetch read it). Each provider plugin's model list is read from the host with a 3 s limit; ChatGPT Web's is a static list. Whether a local driver's run still asks DeepSeek for a session title, and which model id it logs, has not been observed yet.

@lisihao/dsh-solar-bench README · How a run is isolated：- Runs boot a generated profile, `solar-bench-run`, holding only `@deepseek-ai/dsh-base` and `@deepseek-ai/dsh-headless`, so the baseline has no third-party plugin. Each plugin under test is linked from the desktop profile's `node_modules`; its variant passes the plugin's own bundle patch as `--patch`.
- Every variant also gets the experiment's shared patches first: the driver patch sets `agent-default-model` to the chosen `{ provider, model }`; unless web tools are allowed, a patch disables the `tool-web` row; when global skills are left out, a patch points the `skill-filesystem` row's `agentsHome` at an empty directory of the experiment, so the skill loader skips `~/.agents/skills` while bundled skills and every other reader of the agents home are unchanged; a smart-scheduling driver adds the chosen scheduling plugins' bundle patches to every variant, baseline included. The plugin test composes the driver, web-off and skills-off patches with the published `dsh` CLI and checks that the model row becomes `deepseek-v4-pro`, `tool-web` becomes disabled and `skill-filesystem` gets the empty `agentsHome`. @lisihao/dsh-solar-bench README · How a run is isolated：The judge of a judged benchmark is one chat-completion request per grade (temperature 0) to the DeepSeek API with the judge model chosen on the form, outside any harness; its tokens and cost are recorded on the run.

Every run starts from a fresh home, so improvement that depends on state carried across runs cannot show inside one experiment; the diagnosis tab's trend is across experiments and plugin versions.

@lisihao/dsh-solar-bench README · Protocol identity：Every item is answered by the DSH agent with this plugin's prompt (a final `ANSWER:` line), so no score compares with a public leaderboard; the page says so once. Each catalog entry is **faithful** (the benchmark's own items and scoring rule), **adapted** (the card names the change), or **diagnostic** (DSH's own tasks). The adapted entries and what changes, checked against their sources on 2026-10-31:

@lisihao/dsh-solar-bench README · Protocol identity：- BFCL v3 `simple`: the call is JSON in the final answer, not a native DSH tool call.
- MMLU-Pro: the answer is read from the `ANSWER:` line, not the official prompt and extraction rule.
- MATH-500: normalized string or numeric equality, stricter than the official symbolic check.
- SimpleQA: the judge is the chosen DeepSeek model; simple-evals grades with `gpt-4.1-2025-04-14` at the pinned commit.
- MT-Bench: the first turn only, judged by the chosen DeepSeek model where the official setup uses GPT-4.
- LongBench v2: the long text is a workspace file the agent reads.
- ChemBench: multiple-choice items only. ScienceQA: text-only items only. RSI-Exam: the 21 tasks that need no GPU and call no model inside the task.

@lisihao/dsh-solar-bench README · Protocol identity：Each experiment's result is then labelled **every item** (faithful, all items run), **sample** (faithful, fewer items than the source's verified count), **sample of an unverified total**, **adapted** or **diagnostic**. The label is derived from the catalog and the sample size, so ledgers are unchanged.

@lisihao/dsh-solar-bench README · Analysis tools for agents：The plugin registers four read-only tools with DSH's tool registry, so an agent in any conversation can query results. They read only the catalog and the ledgers, so none can start, stop or resume a run, or call a model; replies are cut at 20,000 characters.

@lisihao/dsh-solar-bench README · Analysis tools for agents：| Tool | Answers |
|---|---|
| `bench_catalog` | Benchmarks by category: runnable or why not, protocol identity, item count, license. |
| `bench_results` | Experiments newest first, optionally for one benchmark, with their settings and scoreboard cells. |
| `bench_compare` | One experiment: each plugin against the baseline (verdict, paired difference and interval, paired and differing tasks), success and end-to-end rates, cost and time, and the result's protocol identity. |
| `bench_trace` | One experiment's runs, unmeasurable and timed-out first: status, grader details, error, parsed answer, tokens, cost, time, tool errors. Recorded fields only, not the run's files. |

@lisihao/dsh-solar-bench README · Data：DSH 3.x ledgers under `$DSH_HOME/bench/` are read only through `lib/cli.js import`, which validates and copies `experiment.json` and `runs.jsonl`.

@lisihao/dsh-solar-bench README · Command line：`lib/cli.js` runs experiment files from a shell, imports DSH 3.x ledgers and lists experiments, as before:

```
PLUGIN=~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/node_modules/@lisihao/dsh-solar-bench
node $PLUGIN/lib/cli.js run experiment.yml            # print the plan; nothing runs (exit 2)
node $PLUGIN/lib/cli.js run experiment.yml --yes --max-usd 1 --prices prices.json
node $PLUGIN/lib/cli.js import ~/.dsh/bench/<id>

@lisihao/dsh-solar-bench README · How it was verified：- **Phase 1 of the roadmap** (2026-10-31, run): `claude/bench-harbor` merged; after the merge all tests passed and the 14-rule mutation pass (including nested protected rows) turned a test red for every rule. Protocol identity, the four agent tools and attempt keeping each have tests; breaking the tools' failed-only default, reply cap, failure ordering and protocol field, and attempt keeping's rename and process stop, turned a test red each time. The plugin test checks through the real host that the four tools register and answer.
- **Unit tests** (`tests/`, Vitest, `pnpm test`, 220 tests at the end of roadmap Phase 2): every answer grader passes a right answer and fails a wrong one on synthetic rows; every runnable adapter builds a gradable task; the dataset cache (seeded sampling across parts, fetching only drawn rows, filters, truncation and format refusal, whole-file joins, retries); the judge request and its pricing; the run manager with a fake launcher (driver and web-off patches before the variant's, scheduling plugins in every variant, a sampled public benchmark graded from the final message, a judged benchmark with its

@lisihao/dsh-solar-bench README · Development：```bash
pnpm install
pnpm check   # build, typecheck, unit tests, plugin test
```

`lib/` is committed because the plugin manager installs from the repository without running build scripts; `pnpm build` regenerates it, and CI fails when it differs from the sources. The source is synced from `incubator/bench` of the DeepSeek Solar Harness V4 workspace (branch `claude/bench-v2`, not published).
